text.p: 3Com Corp chairman and chief executive Eric Benhamou said 3Com has implemented the largest internal reorganization in its 17 years to concentrate on corporate and emerging small business and consumer markets.

Benhamou said at an evening reception for media at his home that the restructuring, due to be formally announced on Tuesday, will split 3Com in two, creating 3Com Systems to concentrate on large customers and 3Com Personal Products, focussing on small businesses and emerging consumer markets.
Previously, he noted, the company had been organized along product lines rather than around its customers.

Benhamou said the restructuring would not require any layoffs or additional staff. The company, which is the world's second-largest networking equipment supplier behind Cisco Systems, employs some 5,300 employees in more than 140 countries and posted fiscal 1996 sales of $2.3 billion.
The restructuring took effect on Monday evening, he said.

Benhamou said the regrouping into customer-focussed accounts would have a major impact on 3Com's business. Veteran executives would assume responsibility for the two operating companies under the new structure. The chief executive recently told Wall Street analysts that 3Com was gaining share in core markets.
